opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research max £20,000; Research and Travel max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months) for New Projects, Acquisitions, Conferences, and Long-Term Research categories; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Not open to individuals developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections; Conferences, Lectures and Publications; Long-Term Research; and Research and Travel grants. Applications considered four times per year (Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer rounds).

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire for the duration of the fellowship

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture (or on Henry Moore specifically for Studios & Gardens fellowships). Senior Fellowships for established scholars. No studio facilities offered.
opportunities.summary: Fellowship programme enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence. Types: Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships, and Senior Fellowships (six weeks). Applications closed for 2026/27; next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50, copies added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines who submitted a dissertation within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertation must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Annual prize awarding two prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. The 2025 round closed (deadline 12 December 2025); submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
